outcome: BLOCK combined B06 client release until cross-process queue loss and quarantine permissions are fixed; prior-B06 compatibility is conditional on server-first rollout

findings.scope: B06 client integrated with concurrent collect/run/sync (B07 boundary)
findings.result: A new event written by a second process while the first awaits a valid partial ACK is overwritten by the first process's whole-queue checkpoint. The event was neither sent nor quarantined.

With umask 022, the .tokenizer directory is 0755 and rejected-usage.jsonl is 0644; retained workspace paths and source event IDs are readable by other local users when the home directory is traversable.

findings.scope: new Agent against immediately preceding bounded B06 server
findings.result: The preceding server returns 400 invalid_json without row for a malformed event string; the new Agent cannot quarantine it, so the good neighbor remains pinned. A strict server-first rollout avoids this compatibility path.

positiveEvidence.realTcpHttpToRouteAndPgProbe: passed: 2 accepted, 1 rejected, duplicate replay, reject-only no write

limitations: This is not an independent different-model-family Evaluator verdict or release approval.
The TCP/HTTP probe invokes the real route function, authentication and PostgreSQL, but not the full Next.js middleware/deployment stack.
The two-process loss probe uses a contract-valid synthetic server ACK; the race is wholly on the local queue and does not depend on PostgreSQL.
The local Node 22 run reuses the main checkout's node_modules rather than a fresh npm ci.
Native Windows, exact-SHA CI, production and power-loss fsync durability were not tested.
